reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. Gate 1: AdminLayout is a Next.js App Router default export — framework-invoked, not explicitly called internally; public/exported API exception applies. Gate 2: No trust_assumptions in BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json; the attack path uses the attacker's own authenticated Supabase session (the deleted admin IS the session holder), not a trusted upstream data source. Gate 3: src/app/dashboard/ is explicitly in scope; admin privilege escalation is listed as a key security concern. Code verified: admin/layout.tsx L18-22 queries members with no .is('deleted_at', null) filter; checkAdmin() at members.ts:65 has the identical missing filter, meaning all admin server actions (updateMemberAdmin, syncAllDiscordRoles, updateStatusesForNewAcademicYear, renameGraduatesToNewFormat) are compoundly affected. An attacker can trigger this via an authenticated Supabase session by accessing /dashboard/admin/* as a soft-deleted admin user (deleted_at set, is_admin not cleared), causing unauthorized retention of full admin privileges — including bulk member updates, Discord role sync, and academic year transitions — until the session expires. Severity remains Medium: exploitation requires the attacker to have previously held admin status, limiting the attack surface, but the bypass window is as long as the Supabase session lifetime.
